name: Arts and Crafts
summary: The craft reform of the Victorian room. Handmade oak furniture shows its joints, a deep inglenook holds the hearth, and one stylised plant pattern runs on the walls or the textiles; low beams and built-in settles make the room honest and warm.

philosophy.core_thesis: A room is honest when every piece is made by hand from local materials and shows how it is made.
design_principles: Show the construction: exposed joints, pegs, beams and hand-wrought hardware.
Use one stylised plant or bird pattern per room, on the paper or on the textiles, not on both.
Build furniture into the room: settles, window seats, dressers and bookcases.
Make the hearth a room in the room: an inglenook with built-in seats.
Keep colours from nature: oak brown, sage green, ochre and madder red.
Run a high picture rail or a plate shelf at about 2/3 of the wall height, so that the ceiling feels low.
Use hammered copper, leaded glass and hand-thrown pottery for the accents.
anti_patterns: Veneer or gloss lacquer that hides the wood

composition.plan_logic: A low room on a grid of exposed beams. The inglenook and built-in pieces form the walls; loose furniture is few and heavy.
composition.focal_point: The inglenook with its hearth, built-in settles and a copper hood on the right wall.

rules.rule: Make the inglenook the focal point and set it under a lowered beam.
Lower the visual ceiling with a picture rail or plate shelf.
rules.value: rail at 2/3 of the wall height

rules.rule: Repeat beams and the slats of chairs and settles at one pitch.
Use one pattern per room and repeat the oak and the copper everywhere.
Make the built-in pieces dominant and the loose furniture secondary.
Frame the inglenook and the window seats with posts and beams.
Show depth through recesses: inglenook, bay and alcove.
Give oak and plain or patterned walls the main share, sage and ochre the textiles, and copper and madder the accents.
Light with lanterns that hang low and table lamps with mica or leaded shades.
Keep the route clear from the door to the hearth and the window seat.

zoning.circulation: A clear route from the door to the inglenook along the beams.

palette.distribution: Oak panelling and a plain or patterned wall above it; sage, olive and ochre textiles; copper, madder red and indigo in the accents.

lighting.strategy: Warm, low pools of light. Lanterns hang low over tables; leaded windows and lamps give coloured, filtered light.
lighting.daylight: Small-paned casement or leaded windows give soft side light; window seats sit in the bays.

layers.source: copper pendant lantern with mica panels
table lamp with a mica or leaded shade
layers.position: on the desk and beside the settle

layers.source: hearth fire or warm wall sconces

materials.finish: Fumed or wax-finished oak, hand-hammered metal, matt glazes.
materials.texture_contrast: Rough brick, hammered metal and handwoven wool against planed oak, at about 1:1.

furniture.silhouette: Rectilinear, solid oak pieces with exposed tenons, slats and corbels; heavy and plain.
furniture.arrangement: Built-in settles and dressers form the room; a few loose chairs and one table stand on a hand-knotted rug.

textiles.pattern: One stylised plant or bird pattern per room, block-printed or woven.
textiles.windows: Plain linen curtains on iron or wood poles, often café curtains on the lower half.

objects.approach: Handmade, useful objects: pottery, copper, books and woven baskets.
objects.grouping: Rows along a plate shelf or a mantel; groups of 3–5.
items: row of plates on a plate shelf

implementation.brief: A low beamed living room with fumed oak panelling to a plate shelf and parchment plaster above. A brick inglenook with two built-in settles and a copper hood stands on the right wall; a Morris chair, an oak table and a hand-knotted rug sit before it.
implementation.image_prompt: Arts and Crafts living room, fumed oak wall panelling to a plate shelf, parchment plaster above, exposed oak ceiling beams, brick inglenook fireplace with built-in oak settles and a hammered copper hood, Morris chair with sage cushions, oak table, hand-knotted rug, leaded glass casement windows with a window seat, copper lantern, art pottery on the shelf, warm low light, handmade, interior photograph
implementation.negative_prompt: Gloss, veneer, chrome, machine ornament, saturated colour, minimal white walls.
implementation.camera: 28 mm lens at 140 cm, three-quarter view toward the inglenook.
implementation.scene_3d: Room 550 x 450 cm, ceiling 260 cm with 15 cm beams at 45 cm. Daylight through leaded glass; one 2400 K lantern at 190 cm; a fire light at 1900 K.

emotion.target_response: Honest warmth: the viewer feels at home in a room where each thing is made with care.

avoid_when: The brief asks for light, white or glossy surfaces.

modifiers.how: Curve the lines, add whiplash plant ornament and stained glass; keep the craft and the one-pattern rule.
Remove the pattern and the copper, paint the walls white and hang the chairs on a peg rail.
